nodes.characterization_summary: CrNiCu ternary alloys form fcc crystals within broad composition space of 0∼40 at.% Cr, 20-100 at.% Ni, and 0-80 at.% Cu with (111) surface selected as active surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the CrNiCu ternary alloys are fcc crystals within a broad composition space of 0∼40 at.% Cr, 20-100 at.% Ni, and 0-80 at.% Cu... the fcc (111) surface of CrNiCu ternary alloy was selected as active surface for further calculations.

nodes.characterization_summary: XGBR models predict hydrogen adsorption energies on CrNiCu (111) fcc-hollow and hcp-hollow sites with RMSE 0.018-0.028 eV and R² 0.96-0.99, ranging from -0.8 to 0.1 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the two XGBR models exhibit high accuracies in the prediction of hydrogen adsorption energies at both fcc-hollow and hcp-hollow sites as the RMSE values and the R² values range from 0.018 to 0.028 eV and from 0.96 to 0.99, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: XGBR model predicts water adsorption energies on CrNiCu with RMSE 0.022-0.027 eV and R² 0.97-0.98; Cr sites show strong adsorption (-0.4 to -0.6 eV) vs weak Ni/Cu sites (0 to -0.15 eV).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 3a shows the predicted results of water adsorption energy, with the RMSE values ranging from 0.022 to 0.027 eV and the R² values ranging from 0.97 to 0.98... Cr sites demonstrate much stronger adsorption, with adsorption energies concentrated between -0.4 and -0.6 eV.

nodes.characterization_summary: Water dissociation energy barriers are 0.53 eV for Cr₉Ni₁₅Cu₂₆L and 0.61 eV for Cr₁₄Ni₂₀Cu₁₆L vs 1.05-1.36 eV for Pt/Ni/Cu.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the calculated energy barriers of water dissociation on these two alloys are significantly reduced to 0.53 and 0.61 eV for Cr₉Ni₁₅Cu₂₆L and Cr₁₄Ni₂₀Cu₁₆L, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: XGBR model for water dissociation energy barrier on CrNiCu improved to RMSE 0.02 eV and R² 0.94 after incorporating hydrogen adsorption energy as input feature.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the training results of the updated XGBR model... demonstrate a significant improvement in accuracies, with the RMSE value reduced to 0.02 and the R² value increased to 0.94.

nodes.characterization_summary: Theoretical exchange current densities of fcc CrNiCu alloys with 10-30 at.% Cr, 30-50 at.% Ni, 20-60 at.% Cu exceed Pt benchmark of 0.6 mA/cm².
nodes.evidence_snippet: screening fcc-phase alloys with the composition of 10-30 at.% Cr, 30-50 at.% Ni, and 20-60 at.% Cu exhibit superior HER activity over Pt.

nodes.characterization_summary: Configuration energy differences within 0.03 eV/atom across 60 surface configurations indicate no element segregation tendency for Cr₉Ni₁₅Cu₂₆ and Cr₁₄Ni₂₀Cu₁₆.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the energy differences among the 60 surface configurations for both alloys are within 0.03 eV/atom, indicating that the two CrNiCu alloys have no obvious tendency of element segregation.

nodes.characterization_summary: At HER potential U < -0.48 V (pH=8.1), Cr₉Ni₁₅Cu₂₆ and Cr₁₄Ni₂₀Cu₁₆ surfaces fully occupied by 8H with OH adsorption unfavorable, showing hydroxyl poisoning resistance.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the surfaces of all four considered alloys are fully occupied by H atoms (8H) at the HER potential (U < -0.48 V), whereas OH adsorption remains energetically unfavorable.
